claims.claim: Owners of connected home devices bought devices containing chips.
Owners of connected home devices place those devices beside their routers.
Owners of connected home devices supply the electricity used by those devices.
The server component of connected appliances is undocumented for owners.
Owners cannot inspect the server component on which their connected appliances depend.
Owners cannot replace the server component on which their connected appliances depend.
Closing a connected-doorbell cloud service can disable alerts, stored clips, or account login.
Closing a connected-thermostat cloud service can disable schedules and automation.
Closing a connected-lighting cloud service can disable shared scenes.
After a connected-appliance cloud shutdown, owners can still operate the appliance by pressing a physical button.
Owners chose affected connected appliances because of functionality provided through their apps.
Connected-home routines, integrations, voice commands, and access rules commonly depend on remote databases.
Some remote-database-dependent connected-home features were included in capabilities customers paid for.
Some connected sensors continue sensing after a cloud shutdown but can no longer report their results.
Vendors may disclose connected appliances’ cloud-service requirements in small print.
Cloud services can provide outside alerts for connected appliances.
Cloud services can coordinate connected devices.
Cloud services can perform computational work that is demanding for connected appliances.
Cloud services can deliver updates to connected appliances.
Small connected appliances can rely on larger servers for computational or operational capacity.
Connected-appliance commands can be transmitted across a home network without depending on the vendor cloud.
Connected appliances can store and execute schedules locally on the device.
Connected-appliance accounts and cryptographic keys can remain under household control.
A documented local interface usable without vendor approval can allow independent software to replace a discontinued connected-appliance app.
With local operation, connected heating, lighting, lock, camera, sensor, and switch products can retain their basic functions after cloud features disappear.
Connected-home hardware eventually fails.
Compatibility support for connected-home devices eventually ends.
Local operation can separate an appliance’s useful life from a vendor’s willingness to continue service, acquisition, or bankruptcy.
Homes are increasingly filling with connected property whose operation is governed as a service.
